summary: Clarify pricing ladder applied to mixed microbatch/streamed job causing unexpected credit allocation
description:
Issue summary:
Orbitlytics reports a finalized invoice that charged a higher-than-expected per-batch rate for a job which included a mix of microbatch and streaming requests. They believe warmup and sampled stream tokens were attributed to the batch ladder instead of the streaming ladder.

Impact:
- Customer reports a $3,800 unexpected billing delta on the March billing cycle.
- Blocking: finance/chargeback reconciliation for month-end close.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant in prod (us-east-1) using reserved hours + burst.
- Job: nightly ingest combining N microbatch embed tasks and several streaming toolcall requests in same submission group.
- Model: gptj-6b-quant-v2 pinned.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Submit a mixed job via our Batch API with header X-Grouping-ID = orbit-20260309
2) Include 3 microbatch embed requests (large payloads) and 2 streaming tool-call requests in the same group window.
3) Observe postback payloads in our billing console and downloaded CSV.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming tokens and toolcall invocations should be classified under streaming rate ladder and billed accordingly. Warmup tokens (kv-cache) should be charged as warmup credits where applicable.

Actual behavior:
- Billing console shows all tokens attributed to the microbatch ladder for the grouping ID and applied the higher microbatch per-unit rate. Audit CSV has postbacks tagged as batch.queue for those stream requests.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- billing_audit_orbit_20260309.csv (attached)
- postback_log_excerpt.txt (attached)
- Console screenshot showing invoice line and rate id

Notes: customer included their expected calculation using streaming rate. Asking for correction or provisional credit while we investigate.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:15 - ECC: Confirmed grouping header present in postback entries, grouping ID matched customer-provided file.
2026-03-10 11:02 - Billing Eng (Marcus Lee): Initial hypothesis - rate-selector may prefer batch ladder when group size > 1 and content-type ambiguous.

2026-03-10 13:40 - SRE (Tomás Rivera): Scheduler logs show scheduler grouped both streaming and non-streaming requests into same dispatch window to exploit packing; postback encoder set queue_type=batch to reduce overhead.
2026-03-10 15:10 - Billing Eng: Found recent deploy that changed postback tag precedence when both 'queue_type' and 'streaming_marker' are present; precedence now favors queue_type if value != null.
2026-03-11 09:20 - Support: Reached out to Orbitlytics requesting raw postback JSON for three sample requests and permission to provisionally credit if misbilling confirmed.
2026-03-11 12:05 - Customer: Provided three raw postbacks and agreed to provisional credit while team investigates.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:30 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thanks for the report — we’ve ingested your CSV and flagged for billing engineering. Can you attach the raw postbacks?
2026-03-10 11:10 - Orbitlytics (Customer): Uploaded postback_log_excerpt.txt. We saw the same grouping used intentionally to reduce latency.

2026-03-10 15:25 - Marcus Lee (Billing Eng): We’re reproducing locally against a staging rate-selector with the exact tag set. Preliminary reproduction matches: when postback contains queue_type=batch and streaming_marker=true, the selector yields batch ladder. Marking as probable cause.
2026-03-11 09:25 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thank you — we’ve asked billing to prepare a provisional credit and will follow up with a remediation plan. SLA window: 24 hours.
2026-03-11 12:10 - Orbitlytics (Customer): Appreciate the quick responses. Provisional credit is acceptable pending root cause.
2026-03-11 14:05 - Evelyn Carter (Assignee): Noted — creating INT ticket for rate-selector config change and rollback plan.
root_cause_hypothesis: Recent rate-selector precedence change means explicit 'queue_type' tag overrides streaming markers; mixed grouping with queue_type=batch causes streaming tokens to be billed at batch ladder rates.
next_steps: Billing Eng to validate on staging with customer sample payloads and confirm repro (target: 2026-03-11 EOD).
If repro confirmed, create hotfix to restore streaming_marker precedence or add explicit ladder_override field (INT ticket created).
Apply provisional credit equal to customer-provided delta pending final reconciliation.
Update docs/console to show precedence rules to avoid customer surprises.
Postmortem and changelog entry after fix and customer confirmation.
outcome_notes: Provisional credit hold requested — finance notified to reserve $3,800 against Orbitlytics account.
INT-5521 created to track rate-selector config roll back and testing.
Customer agreed to wait for fix before invoice adjustment; will confirm after remediation.
